verdicts.claim: Checkpointing transfers committed transactions from the WAL file back into the original database file.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file and transfers it back into the original database file."

verdicts.claim: By default, SQLite triggers an automatic checkpoint when the WAL file reaches a threshold of 1,000 pages.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages."

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints are exclusively performed in PASSIVE mode.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE."

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE checkpointing is non-blocking and may not run to completion if concurrent readers or writers are active.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html says long readers prevent checkpoint completion; c3ref (not cited here) states it verbatim: "passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers."

verdicts.claim: FULL checkpoint mode blocks until all concurrent readers and writers have finished (or a timeout occurs) to ensure all WAL
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: FULL "blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot"; imprecise: readers need only reach latest snapshot, not finish.

verdicts.claim: RESTART checkpoint mode behaves like FULL but also resets the WAL index to frame 1, allowing subsequent writes to overwrite
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL ... This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning"; dev.to: "reset the WAL index to frame 1".

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE checkpoint mode behaves like RESTART but additionally truncates the WAL file on disk to zero bytes.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return."

verdicts.claim: Read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows because readers must check the WAL ... proportional to the WAL size.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows in size ... the time needed to check the WAL file is proportional to the size of the WAL file."

verdicts.claim: Long-lived read transactions can cause 'checkpoint starvation' where the checkpointer cannot advance past the oldest active
verdicts.evidence: litestream: "WAL can grow unbounded if read transactions prevent checkpointing"; dev.to: "a single long-running read query or unclosed connection will stall all checkpoints."

verdicts.evidence: Data loss/corruption supported by Tailscale, but fix version is wrong. sqlite.org/wal.html: "It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later." Tailscale: fix first shipped in 3.52.0 (withdrawn), then "published 3.51.3". Draft says 3.53.0.
